items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: I remember once that I played the part of Dr. Rank in A Doll's House.

ctx.x: But Mr. Drury was so smart. And I've always had... The one thing he was adamant about, he wanted us to be able to enter any college in the United States. He said, "If you get the right grades and you have the right classes, you can enter any college in the United States." Because we had an A-program, and he knew it. Now, he was the head of the whole academic thing, so he stressed that with us.

He even taught us Drama! And he taught us just like any Drama teacher. I remember once that I played the part of Dr. Rank in A Doll's House. And he told me something that influenced me later in life. He said a doctor, if he gets complicated, never loses his dignity, and he'll always walk up straight... You won't never see no doctor fallin' all over everybody and stumblin', but he'll always try to use his dignity to stand up straight. He can be drunk... And Dr. Rank was a drunkard, you know. And I had to play this…
But I remembered all them thing later in life, you know. Because I think teachers are the greatest influence on anybody's life. Because I had one or two teachers...
